title: Combo Facts
subtitle: + − × ÷ mixed, every level
bounds: Facts bounds (PROTOCOL 4c): each tier is 10 each of 'a + b = ?', 's − a = ?', 'a × b = ?', 'p ÷ a = ?', every operation in its own cartridge's band at that tier. Add/subtract: sum or minuend 2-10, 11-20, 21-40, 41-70, 71-100 (operands >= 1 on T1, >= 2 after; T2 min operand <= 9, 60% one digit + one digit crossing ten; T3-T5 >= half regroup, >= a quarter two-digit + one-digit, <= a quarter multiples of 10). Multiply/divide: larger factor 1-5, 6-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-15 (factors >= 1 on T1, >= 2 after), divide reads the multiplication fact backwards. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers <= 999, >= 2 near the answer, at most 1 far; answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each per tier; add/subtract T3-T5 and multiply/divide T4-T5 carry a wrong choice sharing the answer's ones digit.

ADD_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Count again: start at the bigger number and count up.
ADD_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted on wrong: the sum is one more or one less than the true sum.

ADD_SUBTRACTED.student: Plus means put together. Add the two numbers, don't take them apart.
ADD_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracted the smaller addend from the larger instead of adding: 8 + 5 = 3.

ADD_NO_CARRY.student: The ones made a new ten. Add that ten in with the tens.
ADD_NO_CARRY.teacher: Dropped the regrouped ten when the ones summed to 10 or more: 38 + 47 = 75.

ADD_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Add the tens, then the ones.
ADD_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Tens digit of the sum is one too many or too few, with the ones right: 34 + 52 = 76 or 96.

SUB_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Check: answer + number taken away must equal the start.
SUB_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted back one step too many or too few: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 1.

SUB_ADDED.student: Take away, don't add. Subtracting makes the number smaller.
SUB_ADDED.teacher: Added the two numbers (s + a) instead of subtracting.

SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.student: Don't flip digits. If the top digit is smaller, trade a ten for 10 ones.
SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.teacher: In each place takes the smaller digit from the larger (14 - 6 gives 12; 52 - 38 gives 26) instead of regrouping.

SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.student: You traded a ten for ones, so the tens digit has to drop by one.
SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.teacher: Regrouped the ones but left the tens unchanged: answer is 10 too big (14 - 6 gives 18; 52 - 38 gives 24).

SUB_TENS_SLIP.student: The tens are off by one ten. Check: answer + taken away = start.
SUB_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 10.

MUL_GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
MUL_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

MUL_ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
MUL_ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

MUL_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
MUL_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

MUL_PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.student: Tens × tens plus ones × ones skips two parts. Split one number, multiply both.
MUL_PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.teacher: Multiplies tens by tens and ones by ones only: 13 × 14 = 100 + 12 = 112.

DIV_GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
DIV_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

DIV_SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. 20 ÷ 5 asks how many 5s fit in 20.
DIV_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

DIV_MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. 20 ÷ 5 asks how many 5s fit in 20.
DIV_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

DIV_TENS_SLIP.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply back to check the size.
DIV_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Quotient off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.
